Extract rules from a catboost model

Source: R/catboost.Model.R
extract_rules.catboost.Model.Rd

Extract interpretable decision rules from a single tree in a CatBoost boosted tree model. Each reachable terminal node (leaf) becomes one rule representing the path from root to that leaf.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'catboost.Model'
extract_rules(x, tree = 1L, data = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A catboost.Model object from the catboost package.

tree

Integer specifying which tree to extract rules from. Uses 1-based indexing (default is 1L). There is one tree per boosting iteration, including for multiclass models.

data

A data frame containing the predictors used to train the model. This is only required when the tree contains categorical splits since catboost stores hashed values instead of the factor levels.

...

Not currently used.

Value

A tibble with class c("rule_set_catboost.Model", "rule_set") and columns:

  • tree: integer, the tree number (matches input parameter).

  • rules: list of R expressions, one per terminal node.

  • id: integer, terminal node ID (1-based).

Details

By default, catboost grows symmetric (oblivious) trees where every node at the same depth uses the same split. For these trees, the leaf id corresponds to catboost's leaf index plus one. Leaves that cannot be reached (e.g., cyl > 7 followed by cyl <= 5) are removed. For trees grown with grow_policy = "Depthwise" or "Lossguide", leaves are numbered from left to right.

Numeric splits send observations with feature <= border to the left and feature > border to the right.

Categorical predictors

One-hot categorical splits (see the one_hot_max_size parameter) become == or %in% conditions.

Most categorical splits use target statistics (CTRs): the levels are converted to numeric values based on the outcome and the split compares that value to a threshold. Since each level always goes to the same side of a split, the split is equivalent to a set of levels. To find these sets, the CTR splits are placed in a separate model that catboost uses to predict every level of the categorical predictor(s) in data. A CTR split then becomes a condition such as g %in% c("b", "c").

catboost can also compute CTRs on combinations of features. These can include several categorical predictors, binned numeric predictors (e.g., x > 0.5), and one-hot indicators. In this case, every combination of levels is evaluated, and the rule is a set of combinations, such as (g == "a" & h %in% c("A", "B")) | (g == "b" & h == "C").

Levels that were not in the training set use a prior value for the CTR. The side of the split that they go to is expressed as the negation of the other side (e.g., !(g %in% c("a", "d"))) so that the rules match how catboost would predict new levels.

Examples

if (rlang::is_installed("catboost")) {
  pool <- catboost::catboost.load_pool(mtcars[, -1], label = mtcars$mpg)
  set.seed(3926)
  fit <- catboost::catboost.train(
    pool,
    params = list(
      iterations = 3,
      depth = 2,
      thread_count = 1,
      logging_level = "Silent",
      allow_writing_files = FALSE
    )
  )

  rules <- extract_rules(fit, tree = 1L)
  rules

  rule_text(rules$rules[[1]])
}
#> [1] "cyl <= 5"
